title: The Monkeys Who Followed the Ancestors

pages.text: Mawuena and her brother Kafu followed their guide, Mr Agbeko, into a patch of forest beside the village of Tafi Atome in the Volta Region. “This is a sacred grove,” he said, “about twenty-eight hectares of forest. In it live our mona monkeys. Please stay on the path, and listen to my instructions.”
sentences: Mawuena and her brother Kafu followed their guide, Mr Agbeko, into a patch of forest beside the village of Tafi Atome in the Volta Region.
“This is a sacred grove,” he said, “about twenty-eight hectares of forest.
In it live our mona monkeys.
Please stay on the path, and listen to my instructions.”
pages.alt: Two children and a guide enter a green forest grove on a path.

pages.text: High in the trees, brown monkeys with pale throats swung and chattered. “Mona monkeys,” whispered Kafu. “Here, we treat them as sacred,” said Mr Agbeko. “We do not hunt them, and we do not harm them. Please do not touch them; wild monkeys can bite, and we want them to stay wild.”

“We do not hunt them, and we do not harm them.
Please do not touch them; wild monkeys can bite, and we want them to stay wild.”
pages.alt: Mona monkeys sit on branches above two children and a guide.

pages.text: “How did they come to be sacred?” asked Mawuena. Mr Agbeko smiled. “Our people say our ancestors came here about two hundred years ago from a place called Assini. They carried an idol, which they placed in the forest. Soon afterwards, villagers saw monkeys they believed had followed them. The monkeys became seen as representatives of the gods.”

Mr Agbeko smiled.

They carried an idol, which they placed in the forest.

The monkeys became seen as representatives of the gods.”
pages.alt: Travellers carry a bundle through a forest while monkeys watch from the trees.

pages.text: “So is it true that the monkeys followed them?” asked Kafu. “That is what the village tells,” said Mr Agbeko. “Nobody can check it with a written record. A scientist might ask other questions: how did the monkeys live here before, and how many came? But for the village, the story is part of who we are.”

pages.alt: A boy asks a question with a speech bubble that has a question mark.

pages.text: Mawuena thought about it. “Whether or not we can prove how the monkeys arrived,” she said, “the belief did something real. It kept people from hunting them and cutting the forest.” “Exactly,” said Mr Agbeko. “A belief can protect nature.” Kafu wrote: belief + care = protection.

“A belief can protect nature.” Kafu wrote: belief + care = protection.
pages.alt: A girl writes a note with an arrow from belief to a healthy forest.

pages.text: “But the protection began to weaken,” said Mr Agbeko. “In the 1980s, some people began to farm and cut trees in the grove. By 1995, the forest was found to be damaged.” Mawuena looked up at the canopy. “What did the village do?” “They talked,” said Mr Agbeko. “And they decided to act together.”
sentences: “But the protection began to weaken,” said Mr Agbeko.
“In the 1980s, some people began to farm and cut trees in the grove.
By 1995, the forest was found to be damaged.” Mawuena looked up at the canopy.
“What did the village do?” “They talked,” said Mr Agbeko.
“And they decided to act together.”
pages.alt: A map shows farms creeping towards the grove with some trees cut.

pages.text: “In 1996, the community began a project with a conservation group,” said Mr Agbeko. “They planted trees around the edge, built a welcome centre, and trained guides like me. Visitors pay, and the money goes to community needs, such as schools, and to the people who gave up farmland for the sanctuary.” Kafu counted his sandals. “So the forest earns its keep!”

pages.alt: Villagers plant young trees along the edge of the forest.

pages.text: At the end of the walk, Mawuena wrote: Told by the village: the monkeys followed the ancestors. Known: the grove shelters mona monkeys, and the village works to protect it. Open: where the monkeys really came from. “Some questions have more than one kind of answer,” said Mr Agbeko, “and one of them is care.” The end.

activities.question: How do the villagers say the monkeys came to Tafi Atome?
options: They followed the ancestors from Assini
They were brought by a trader on a boat

activities.prompt: The grove started to be damaged. What could help save it?
options: The community working together to protect and replant it

activities.question: How does tourism help the village, according to Mr Agbeko?
options: The money goes to community needs and landowners who gave up farmland
It pays for the guide to travel abroad

activities.definition: Very special and holy, deserving great respect.

activities.prompt: Put the story of the grove in order.
items: The ancestors came with an idol.
Monkeys were seen in the forest and treated as sacred.
The community started to protect and replant it.
